{{Short description|American mathematician (1938–2026)}}
{{Use American English|date=July 2026}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=September 2021}}
[[File:Robert Plemmons.jpg|thumb|Plemmons in 2007]]

'''Robert James Plemmons''' (December 18, 1938 – February 6, 2026) was an American mathematician who specialized in [[computational mathematics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Nagy|first1=James|last2=Ng|first2=Michael|date=July 2, 2015|title=Dedication to Robert J. Plemmons|journal=Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications|volume=22|issue=5|pages=793–794|doi=10.1002/nla.2002|s2cid=206314486 |issn=1070-5325}}</ref> He was the emeritus Z. Smith Reynolds Professor of Mathematics and Computer Science at [[Wake Forest University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://college.wfu.edu/cs/people/cs-faculty|title=Faculty – Department of Computer Science|website=college.wfu.edu|access-date=August 9, 2018}}</ref> In 1979, Plemmons co-authored the book ''Nonnegative Matrices in the Mathematical Sciences''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://www.elsevier.com/books/nonnegative-matrices-in-the-mathematical-sciences/berman/978-0-12-092250-5|title=Nonnegative Matrices in the Mathematical Sciences, 1st Edition|last1=Berman|first1=Abraham|last2=Plemmons|first2=Robert J.|publisher=Academic Press|year=1979|isbn=9781483260860}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Plemmons was born on December 18, 1938, in the small town of [[Old Fort, North Carolina]], and grew up in rural Appalachia.<ref name=":0" /> He attended Old Fort High School and graduated in 1957, having been the star athlete in both baseball and football.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/arrowhead19571957oldf|title=The Arrowhead [1957]|last=Old Fort High School (Old Fort|first=N. C. )|date=1957|others=McDowell County Public Library}}</ref>

He attended [[Wake Forest University]] (WFU) on a full baseball scholarship.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www4.ncsu.edu/~njrose/Special/DeptHistory/1980-1989.html|title=Math Dept History: 1980–1989|website=www4.ncsu.edu|access-date=August 9, 2018|archive-date=September 6, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080906173926/http://www4.ncsu.edu/~njrose/Special/DeptHistory/1980-1989.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Former athletic director [[Gene Hooks]] was his baseball coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://gastoniagazette.newspaperarchive.com/gastonia-gazette/1959-04-09/page-11/|title=Gene Says Deacs Set for Grind|date=April 9, 1959|work=The Gastonia Gazette|page=11}}</ref> In 1959, he held the record for [[earned run average]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/wake/sports/m-basebl/auto_pdf/bb44to55.pdf|title=Wake Forest Baseball, 2002 Media Guide|date=2002|access-date=August 21, 2018|archive-date=August 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822113417/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/wake/sports/m-basebl/auto_pdf/bb44to55.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the years 1959–61, he held the record for victories, [[innings]] pitched, [[strikeout]]s, and complete games, and made All-Conference Pitcher all three years.<ref name=":4" /> In the academic year 1960–61, he was awarded the WFU ACC Scholar-Athlete of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sass/acc-scholar-athlete.html|title=Wake Forest SASS – WakeForestSports.com – The Official Site of Demon Deacon Athletics|website=www.wakeforestsports.com|access-date=August 9, 2018}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://library.digitalnc.org/cdm/singleitem/collection/yearbooks/id/1811/rec/59|title=The Howler [1961] :: North Carolina College and University Yearbooks|website=library.digitalnc.org|access-date=August 9, 2018}}</ref> Plemmons graduated from Wake Forest in 1961 with a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics.<ref name=":0" />

During the early 1960s, Plemmons played professional baseball for four years with the [[Baltimore Orioles]]' minor league clubs.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Orioles Sign Old Fort's Bob Plemmons|last=Terrell|first=Bob|date=June 4, 1961|work=Asheville Citizen – Times (Sports)}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z0hkCwAAQBAJ&q=robert+plemmons+baseball&pg=PT163|title=Tales from the Wake Forest Demon Deacons Locker Room: A Collection of the Greatest Demon Deacon Stories Ever Told|last=Collins|first=Dan|date=January 19, 2016|publisher=Skyhorse Publishing, Inc.|isbn=9781613218518}}</ref> He played with the [[Tri-City Atoms]], [[Aberdeen Pheasants]], and [[Elmira Pioneers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/register/player.fcgi?id=plemmo001rob|title=Robert Plemmons Minor Leagues Statistics & History {{!}} Baseball-Reference.com|website=Baseball-Reference.com|access-date=August 9, 2018}}</ref>

In December 1963, he married Mary Jo Harris, also from Old Fort and a graduate of Old Fort High School.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Plemmons attended graduate school at [[Auburn University]] from 1961 to 1965, receiving his PhD in [[applied mathematics]] in 1965.<ref name=":0" /> He then held research positions with [[Martin Marietta]] in [[Orlando, Florida]], and the [[National Security Agency]] in [[Fort George G. Meade|Ft. Meade]].<ref name=":0" /> He served as a faculty member at the [[University of Mississippi]] from 1966 to 1967,<ref name=":6" /> before moving to the [[University of Tennessee|University of Tennessee Knoxville]] in 1967.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6" /> In 1981, Plemmons moved to [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], where he taught at [[North Carolina State University]] until 1990.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6" /> While there, he founded the University of North Carolina System's Center for Research in Scientific Computation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www4.ncsu.edu/~njrose/Special/Tidbits/CRSC.html|title=Center for Research in Scientific Computation|website=www4.ncsu.edu|access-date=August 9, 2018|archive-date=February 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201004327/http://www4.ncsu.edu/~njrose/Special/Tidbits/CRSC.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Plemmons joined the faculty of [[Wake Forest University]] in 1990.<ref name=":0" /> In 2013, he retired from teaching,<ref name=":7">{{Cite news|url=http://research.wfu.edu/files/2014/02/2013-Annual-Report.pdf|title=2013 Annual Report|date=2013|work=Office of Research and Sponsored Programs, Wake Forest University}}</ref> but still conducted research at WFU.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Chan|first1=Raymond H.|last2=Kan|first2=Kelvin K.|last3=Nikolova|first3=Mila|author3-link=Mila Nikolova|last4=Plemmons|first4=Robert J.|date=June 3, 2018|title=A two-stage method for spectral-spatial classification of hyperspectral images|journal=Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision |volume=62 |issue=6–7 |page=790 |doi=10.1007/s10851-019-00925-9 |arxiv=1806.00836|bibcode=2020JMIV...62..790C }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://college.wfu.edu/cs/graduate-program/prospective-students/185-2|title=Reasons To Join Us – Department of Computer Science|website=college.wfu.edu|access-date=August 9, 2018|archive-date=August 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819161817/http://college.wfu.edu/cs/graduate-program/prospective-students/185-2|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also the professor and mentor of former NBA and WFU basketball player [[Rusty LaRue]].<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite journal|date=December 1995|title=Triple Threat|url=https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/handle/10339/58207|journal=Wake Forest University Magazine|pages=32|via=Wake Forest University}}</ref>

== Academic work ==
Plemmons focused his work on applied [[computational mathematics]].<ref name=":0" /> At [[Auburn University|Auburn]] in the early 1960s, Plemmons' work with PhD advisors Richard Ball and Emilie Haynsworth<ref name=":0" /> was focused on [[Finite Semigroup (mathematics)|finite semigroups]] theory.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Plemmons|first1=R.J.|last2=Tamura|first2=T.|date=1965|title=Semigroups with a maximal homomorphic image having zero|journal=Proc. Japan Acad.|volume=41|issue=8|pages=681–685|doi=10.3792/pja/1195522294|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Plemmons|first=R. J.|date=1967|title=On computing non-equivalent finite algebraic systems|journal=Math. Algebra|volume=2|pages=80–84}}</ref> He continued this research until the early 1980s at the [[University of Tennessee|University of Tennessee Knoxville]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Harrod|first1=W.|last2=Plemmons|first2=R. J.|date=1984|title=Comparison of some direct methods for computing stationary distributions of Markov chains|journal=SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput.|volume=5|issue=2|pages=453–469|doi=10.1137/0905033}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Plemmons|first=R. J.|date=1973|title=Regular nonnegative matrices|journal=Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=39|pages=26–32|doi=10.1090/s0002-9939-1973-0313274-6|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 1979, he co-authored the book Nonnegative Matrices in the Mathematical Sciences along with Abraham Berman.<ref name=":1" /> The book has been cited over 7,500 times.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?&as_sdt=0,34&q=non+negative+matrices+in+the+mathematical+sciences&btnG=|title=Google Scholar|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=August 9, 2018}}</ref> In 1994, it was revised and republished by the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Nonnegative Matrices in the Mathematical Sciences|last1=Berman|first1=Abraham|last2=Plemmons|first2=Robert J.|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|year=1994|isbn=9780898713213|doi=10.1137/1.9781611971262}}</ref>

In the mid-to-late 1980s until mid-1990s, his research focused on numerical linear algebra,<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Birth of Numerical Analysis, Volume 10|last1=Bultheel|first1=A.|author1-link= Adhemar Bultheel |last2=Cools|first2=R.|author-link2=Roshan Cools |last3=Chen|first3=D.|last4=Plemmons|first4=P.|publisher=World Scientific|year=2010|isbn=978-9812836250|pages=109–140|chapter=Nonnegativity constraints in numerical analysis}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Henkel|first1=C.S.|last2=Plemmons|first2=R.J.|date=1991|title=Parallel recursive least squares on a hypercube multiprocessor, in: Numerical Linear Algebra, Digital Signal Processing and Parallel Algorithms|journal=NATO ASI Series|volume=Ser. F 70|pages=571–577}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Berry|first1=M.W.|last2=Plemmons|first2=R.J.|date=1985|title=Computing a banded basis of the null space on the Denelcor HEP multiprocessor, in: Proceedings of the AMS/SIAM Conference on the Role of Linear Algebra in Systems Theory, Bowdoin, ME, USA|journal=Contemporary Mathematics|volume=47|pages=7–23|doi=10.1090/conm/047/02}}</ref> specifically in [[Matrix theory (physics)|Matrix Theory]] with applications in [[Markov chain|Markov]] chains and nonnegative matrices.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kontovasilis|first1=K.|last2=Plemmons|first2=R.J.|last3=Stewart|first3=W.J.|date=1991|title=Block cyclic SOR for Markov chains with p-cyclic infinitesimal generator|journal=Linear Algebra Appl.|volume=154–156|pages=145–223|doi=10.1016/0024-3795(91)90377-9|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Barker|first1=G.|last2=Plemmons|first2=R.J.|date=1986|title=Convergent iterations for computing stationary distributions of Markov chains|journal=SIAM J. Algebr. Discrete Methods|volume=7|issue=3|pages=390–398|doi=10.1137/0607044}}</ref> Plemmons has been recognized internationally for his significant contributions to the field, celebrated at the Linear Algebra: Theory, Applications, and Computations Conference held at [[Wake Forest University]] in 1999 in honor of Plemmons' 60th birthday,<ref name=":0" /> and the International Workshop on Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications held in Hong Kong in 2013 in honor of his 75th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.cuhk.edu.hk/conference/nlaa2013/|title=CUHK :: Math :: International Workshop on Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications (November 17–18, 2013)|website=www.math.cuhk.edu.hk|access-date=August 18, 2018}}</ref>

Plemmons conducted research in imaging physics and applied optics at [[Wake Forest University|Wake Forest]] from the late 1990s.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last=Stock-Windsor|first=Christina|title=A Clear View of Forever|url=https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/handle/10339/58216|journal=Wake Forest Magazine|date=March 1997|volume=March 1997|pages=19–23}}</ref> He focused initially in [[biometrics]], including [[iris recognition]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Handbook of Iris Recognition|last1=Jillela|first1=R.|last2=Ross|first2=A.|last3=Boddeti|first3=N.|last4=Vijaya Kumar|first4=B.|last5=Hu|first5=X.|last6=Plemmons|first6=R.J.|last7=Pauca|first7=P.|publisher=Springer|year=2016|isbn=978-1447167846|editor-last=Bowyer|editor-first=K|pages=281–308|chapter=Chapter 13: Iris Segmentation for Challenging Periocular Images|editor-last2=Burge|editor-first2=M.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Gracht|first1=Joseph van der|last2=Pauca|first2=V. Paul|last3=Setty|first3=Harsha|last4=Narayanswamy|first4=Ramkumar|last5=Plemmons|first5=Robert|last6=Prasad|first6=Sudhakar|last7=Torgersen|first7=Todd|editor-first1=Zia-ur |editor-first2=Robert A. |editor-first3=Stephen E. |editor-last1=Rahman |editor-last2=Schowengerdt |editor-last3=Reichenbach |date=July 15, 2004|title=Visual Information Processing XIII|chapter=Iris recognition with enhanced depth-of-field image acquistion |volume=5438|pages=120–129|doi=10.1117/12.542151|s2cid=2552897}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Hu|first1=X.|last2=Pauca|first2=P.|last3=Plemmons|first3=R.J.|title=Biometric Recognition |chapter=Iterative Directional Ray-Based Iris Segmentation for Challenging Periocular Images |date=2011|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science|volume=LNCS7098|pages=91–99|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-25449-9_12|isbn=978-3-642-25448-2}}</ref> His later research was in space situational awareness, tracking [[space debris]] using optical methods to prevent damage to space assets.<ref name=":9" />

Over the years, he received funding from the [[National Science Foundation]], the [[National Security Agency]], the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], the [[NATO|North Atlantic Treaty Organization]], the [[Air Force Office of Scientific Research]], the [[Army Research Office]], the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]], the [[Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity]], and the [[National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency]].<ref name=":7" /> His research was continuously funded by the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] from 1973.<ref name=":10">{{Cite news|title=What Does the Government Get For Its Investment in Basic Research?|date=1996|work=SIAM News}}</ref>

In 1996, Plemmons delivered a congressional testimony to the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] Committee on National Security,<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":11">United States. Cong. House. Subcommittee on National Security. Committee on Appropriations. ''Testimony on FY 1997 Appropriations for the Department of Defense. May 1, 1996.'' Chaired by the Hon. C.W. Bill Young. 104th Cong. 2nd sess. Washington: GPO, 1996 (statement of&nbsp;Robert J. Plemmons, Wake Forest University Professor, Representative of the Joint Policy Board for Mathematics).</ref>   in support of appropriations to the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] on behalf of the [[Joint Policy Board for Mathematics]], including the [[American Mathematical Society]] and [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]].<ref name=":11" />

The mathematics lineage of Plemmons can be traced back to the German mathematicians in the 17th century.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=11324|title=Robert Plemmons – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=August 19, 2018}}</ref> Among his peers, he was a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2013#Robert_J._Plemmons|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2013|website=siam.org}}</ref>

He was the author of more than 250 publications on [[computational mathematics]],<ref name=":8" /> and served on the [[editorial board]] of six journals.<ref name=":3" />

== Death ==
Plemmons died from cancer at his home in [[Winston-Salem, North Carolina]], on February 6, 2026, at the age of 87.<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert James Plemmons |url=https://www.salemfh.com/obituaries/Robert-James-Plemmons?obId=47194198 |website=Salem Funerals & Cremations |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref>
